# QR Statistics / Domain Knowledge Oral

[← Two Sigma](../README.md) · [Every Two Sigma question](../../two-sigma.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/qr-statistics-domain-oral)

`expected-value` `linear-algebra` `linear-regression` `math-reasoning` `probability`

---

## Requirements

Be ready for verbal and whiteboard derivations covering statistics and domain-specific subjects. Reported prompts include:

- A Markov-chain problem in which an approximation was turned down, an exact analytical result was requested, and the work produced a cubic equation.
- Testing whether a pairwise correlation matrix is feasible: determine the allowable range of correlation `p` for variables `x, y, z`, using determinant, eigenvalue, or cosine-theta arguments, then extend the reasoning to `n` variables.
- Find the covariance of the maximum and minimum among `n` i.i.d. Uniform(0, 1) variables through `E[XY] - E[X]E[Y]` and an integral over their joint distribution.
- Explain omitted-variable bias in regression, including its effect on beta and a proof in matrix notation.
- In a complete graph whose edges have independent continuous random weights, a pair `(a, b)` is good when each endpoint is the other endpoint's highest-weight neighbor; determine the expected count of good pairs.
- A detailed discussion of the resume or research area when the interviewer has a similar background.

## Notes

- Depending on the interview loop, this round may be described as statistics, domain knowledge, or core statistics.
- The best responses establish distributions, constraints, and equations early; vague machine-learning intuition is insufficient.
- When an exact form is requested, do not end with simulation or approximation unless the interviewer approves it.

## Preparation

- Revisit the linear-algebra requirements for legitimate correlation matrices, including positive-semidefinite conditions, eigenvalue tests, and determinant checks.
- Work through joint order-statistic distributions for uniform-variable minima and maxima.
- Rehearse omitted-variable bias in both scalar and matrix forms.
- Practice small graph expectation problems with indicator variables and linearity of expectation.
